purpose: Insulin lispro-aabc is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults and children with diabetes. It works around mealtime to prevent your blood sugar from going too high after you eat. It can be used in people with both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes.
how_it_works: This is a fast-acting form of insulin that works similarly to the insulin your body naturally makes after a meal. It helps move sugar from your blood into your body's cells, where it can be used for energy. Because it starts working very quickly — usually within about 15 minutes — you take it right at the start of a meal or within 20 minutes of eating.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can cause shakiness, sweating, dizziness, hunger, or confusion. You may also notice redness, swelling, or itching at the injection site. Weight gain can also happen over time with insulin use.
warnings: Never share your insulin pen or needles with anyone else, even if the needle has been changed — this can spread serious infections. Do not use this insulin if your blood sugar is already too low. If you are sick, stressed, or changing your diet or exercise routine, your insulin needs may change — talk to your doctor. Alcohol can affect your blood sugar when using insulin, so use caution. Always carry a fast-acting sugar source (like glucose tablets or juice) in case your blood sugar drops too low.
typical_dosing: Your dose is individualized by your doctor based on your blood sugar levels, diet, and other factors. Generally, you inject it right at the start of your meal or up to 20 minutes after you begin eating. It is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) in the stomach area, upper arm, or thigh. Rotate your injection sites each time to keep the skin healthy. Never adjust your dose on your own without checking with your healthcare provider first.
